newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 1996 tax haul seen NLG 4.5 bln over estimate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 1996 tax haul seen NLG 4.5 bln over estimate.

text.p: Provisional figures indicate that Dutch tax revenues for 1996 will turn out some 4.5 billion guilders higher than the government had previously estimated, a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said on Monday.
"The figures are very provisional and we've only just started to analyse them, but at the moment they indicate a revenue windfall of about 4.5 billion," she said.
Analysis was needed, among other things, to determine the extent to which revenues which might otherwise have been received in 1997 had already been collected in 1996, she added.
Dutch media said the higher than expected tax revenues were caused by strong economic growth and measures to stamp out tax evasion, but the spokeswoman was unwilling to comment on this.

Politicians of the ruling Labour, Liberal and D66 parties were quoted in the media as saying that most of the extra tax income should be used to set up a fund which would help meet the spiralling costs of the state old-age pension scheme.
But the opposition Christian Democrats were quoted as saying that priority should be given to further reducing the government's budget deficit.
The budget published last September estimated central government revenues at 188.4 billion guilders and spending at 201.9 billion in 1996.
The government deficit, according to the EMU definition, was estimated at 2.6 percent of GDP in 1996 and 2.2 percent in 1997.
